problem: Underwater exploration systems such as CORAL build BEV occupancy maps indirectly (monocular depth, 3D unprojection, rasterization), and depth errors from scattering and attenuation propagate into the navigation map. Learned BEV occupancy predictors are trained for IoU, which does not reflect how spatial errors affect planning.
motivation: Navigation needs obstacles localized accurately enough to avoid and targets accurately enough to approach, and IoU scores a cell right or wrong regardless of its distance from the truth. The authors observe that direct substitution of a learned BEV occupancy model into a navigation stack is not enough, so they decompose the output into planner-relevant fields and supervise them with spatially calibrated losses.
key_idea: Replace CORAL's depth-based perception front end with a direct monocular RGB-to-BEV predictor that outputs separate structure, target and observability fields, trained with transport-style spatial objectives and structure distillation.
insight: Spatial supervision matters more than architectural changes: of 17 architectural variants only an auxiliary range classification loss helped, by about +0.9 structure IoU, while the planner-aware losses lifted structure IoU from 29.47 to 37.39 and target IoU from 46.39 to 52.74. Higher IoU is not the whole story, since GaussianFormer has a 0.10 m same-bearing range error despite weaker IoU. Error analysis shows structure false positives are mostly range errors (53-70%) and target false positives mostly lateral extent (48-78%), which motivates radial and target-extent losses. The occupancy anchor is necessary: removing it drops occupancy IoU from 37.9 to 20.4.
method: Planner-ready BEV heads: keeps the AquaBEV trunk (polar queries, causal range reasoning, Cartesian reconstruction) and predicts three independent sigmoid fields (structure, target, observability) that overlap freely. They are routed to the obstacle map, semantic map and explored-area map respectively.
Occupancy anchor loss: L2 between the occupancy logit and that of a frozen original AquaBEV, weight 1.0, to prevent geometry drift during adaptation.
Radial transport loss: 1D Earth Mover distance along each ray on per-ray normalized structure mass, penalizing range displacement of obstacles.
Spatial false-positive target loss: penalizes false positive target mass by its distance to the nearest true target cell (capped at D_max).

Target transport loss: normalized target distributions compared along range and azimuth, with angular error converted to metres at a 5 m reference range, so it measures displacement independent of mass.

Structure distillation: a frozen teacher RayOccNet that receives GT depth transfers polar structure logits to the RGB student, with a range weighting (1+r/5) emphasizing far structure. The teacher is discarded at inference.
CORAL integration: the local fields are transformed with pose T_t and accumulated into CORAL's persistent maps. VLM reasoning, verification, planning and control are unchanged.

setting.backbone: AquaBEV (polar-query monocular RGB-to-BEV network) fine-tuned with planner-aware losses, inside the CORAL stack (VLM planner unchanged)
setting.training_data: CORAL Blender reef dataset: 2,945 RGB frames across 10 environments (train 1,978 / val 494 / test 473 frames), initialized from real-world AquaBEV checkpoints, 25 epochs, 3 seeds. Pool model initialized from uScenes weights and adapted with simulation data.
setting.observation: monocular front-facing RGB plus vehicle pose
setting.action_space: waypoints from CORAL's VLM planner with dynamics-aware local trajectory generation
setting.simulator: Blender reef environments (CORAL); physical pool with BlueROV2 Heavy
setting.privileged: Simulator segmentation used for target semantics in closed loop; GT depth for the teacher during training only; sonar provides the obstacle map for the local planner in real-world trials

numbers.eval_set_note: ten simulated reef environments, closed-loop exploration
numbers.backbone: AquaBEV-Nav front end + CORAL VLM planner
numbers.extra: perception front end replaced only; simulator segmentation used for target semantics

numbers_note: Real-world pool evaluation is qualitative only, with no numbers. Table perception says 37.48 structure IoU while the loss ablation shows 37.39. The split label 'test' is inferred from the test environments, though the text also mentions validation trajectories for accumulation.
results: AquaBEV-Nav reaches 37.48 structure IoU and 53.2 target IoU, beating AquaBEV (29.9 / 46.6). In closed-loop simulation it reaches 88.95% coverage with zero collisions, versus 59.58% for CORAL with DAv2 and 68.33% for the best learned baseline, TPVFormer. The original CORAL reports 94.28% under its own configuration, which is higher.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulated reefs and a controlled pool; real-world results are qualitative with no ground truth
Closed-loop coverage (88.95%) is still below the original CORAL's reported 94.28%, and completion time is longer than CORAL (DA2) (734 s vs 620 s)
Uncertainty is not exposed to the planner and long-horizon error accumulation in memory is not studied
